subject: music
title: Development and Recapitulation
welcome_lead: The middle that fragments and the return that resolves.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: sonata-form development and recapitulation.
final_note: Sonata form ends where it began — but transformed.

concepts.def: Central section: motivic fragmentation, distant keys, tension.
Final section: both subjects return, now in tonic.
Second subject re-presented in tonic, resolving exposition's contrast.
Apparent return in wrong key — Haydn's joke device.
End of development poised on V, preparing tonic's return.

walkthroughs.body_html: The development takes motifs from the exposition and transforms them — sequencing, fragmenting, inverting, modulating through distant keys. Tension builds toward a dominant pedal preparing return.
The recapitulation brings back first subject in tonic and — crucially — second subject also in tonic (resolving exposition's tonal contrast). Transitions adjust to remain in tonic.
Beethoven expanded the coda into a near-second development (Symphony 3 'Eroica', 1804). Earlier sonatas often ended briefly after recapitulation.

options: Music played in a circle.
Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).
